original_question: Determine whether there exists a group von Neumann algebra L(G) that is pseudocompact, and whether there exists an icc non inner amenable group von Neumann algebra L(G) that is not pseudocompact.
target_in_paper: Problem 4 in the section "Matrix ultraproducts," read together with Problem 3, which gives the paper’s definition of "pseudocompact." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the exact two-part existence question posed in Problem 4: first, whether some group von Neumann algebra is pseudocompact; second, whether some group von Neumann algebra coming from an icc non-inner-amenable group fails to be pseudocompact. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The draft omits the paper-specific definition of "pseudocompact." In Problem 3, a non-Gamma factor M is called pseudocompact if there exists a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N such that M is elementarily equivalent to the tracial matrix ultraproduct ∏_U M_n(C). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Because the paper introduces pseudocompactness only for non-Gamma factors, the standalone version should explicitly say that the question uses "pseudocompact" in the sense of Problem 3, or else build that non-Gamma II_1-factor scope into the formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The ambient ultraproduct data should be made explicit: U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, M_n(C) denotes the complex n-by-n matrix algebra, and the relevant ultraproduct is the tracial matrix ultraproduct. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The draft leaves implicit that elementary equivalence is being taken in the first-order framework of tracial von Neumann algebras, as set up in the paper’s opening notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

In the second clause, the hypotheses "icc" and "non-inner amenable" are hypotheses on the group G whose group von Neumann algebra is L(G), not properties of the algebra itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Does there exist a group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is a pseudocompact non-Gamma II_1 factor, in the sense that there exists a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N for which L(G) is elementarily equivalent, as a tracial von Neumann algebra, to the tracial matrix ultraproduct ∏_U M_n(C)? Moreover, does there exist an icc, non-inner-amenable group G such that L(G) is not pseudocompact in this sense? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 4 itself, not a broader neighboring issue, because it reproduces the same two existence clauses appearing there. To make it stand-alone without changing scope, the only additions needed are the immediately preceding definition of pseudocompact from Problem 3 and the opening notation specifying ultrafilters, tracial matrix ultraproducts, and elementary equivalence. No explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 4 is supplied nearby in the paper, so none should be added. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
